decisions.reason: 'your apartment' in turn 1 is a definite possessive that directly presupposes B has an apartment.

decisions.claim: B has not moved out of their apartment
decisions.reason: 'You should have moved out long, long ago' is a counterfactual modal presupposing B has NOT moved out (the action was not completed).

decisions.claim: B endures/stands the heat in their apartment
decisions.reason: 'how can you stand the heat' presupposes B is enduring the heat. The location (apartment) is contextually linked from turn 1.

decisions.claim: B does not have air-conditioning in their apartment
decisions.reason: 'Don't you have air-conditioning' is a negative question that presupposes the absence of AC in B's apartment. Turn 3 ('I guess not') confirms A's expectation was met.

decisions.claim: B has been living in their apartment for a long time
decisions.reason: 'long, long ago' in the counterfactual 'should have moved out' presupposes B has been living there for a long time.

decisions.claim: B experiences heat in their apartment
decisions.reason: 'B experiences heat in their apartment' is a weaker projection of 'B endures/stands the heat in their apartment' (c3). Same evidence, same location, c3 is more complete.
